output.understanding: Smoke test of the orchestration pipeline on a trivial, low-risk task: create a new test file `orchestrator/test/util.test.mjs` using the built-in `node:test` runner, covering the exported `slugify()` and `truncate()` helpers from `orchestrator/util.mjs`. Strictly additive — no existing file may be modified. Verification is `npm test` passing. No product decision is involved, so no human input is required.
scope: Unit tests for slugify(): typical strings, spaces/punctuation, casing, accents/unicode if supported, empty string, and other edge cases actually observable from util.mjs behavior
Unit tests for truncate(): string shorter than limit, equal to limit, longer than limit (including suffix/ellipsis behavior as implemented), zero/small limits, empty string
Use node:test (test/describe/it) with node:assert/strict, matching the idiom of any existing tests in the repo
Verify the full suite passes via `npm test` with no regressions
out_of_scope: Any modification to orchestrator/util.mjs (including 'obvious' bug fixes — report instead)
Modifying package.json, test scripts, CI config, or any other existing file
Adding test frameworks, assertion libraries, or any new dependency
Tests for other helpers/modules in the orchestrator
Refactoring, renaming, or restructuring existing code or test layout
Documentation, ROADMAP or feature work beyond the smoke test
priorities: 1. Read util.mjs first and test the actual implemented behavior — never assume semantics; document real behavior, do not encode wishful behavior
2. Strictly additive change: exactly one new file created, zero files modified
3. `npm test` passes cleanly, including all pre-existing tests
4. Tests are deterministic, dependency-free, and readable; clear test names per case
5. If util.mjs appears buggy or the helpers are not exported, report it in the summary and escalate rather than editing util.mjs
constraints: Only `node:test` and `node:assert` — no new dependencies (a new dependency would be REQUIRES_BRAIN_APPROVAL and is rejected in advance for this run)
Node >= 22; orchestrator has no runtime dependencies — keep it that way
Exactly one file created: orchestrator/test/util.test.mjs; any other file touched is out of scope and must be escalated
Test command is `npm test` — do not change it
Work on a feature branch per the standard flow; no force-push, no history rewrite
Keep the run small: this is a pipeline smoke test, not a testing-coverage initiative
